title: Regional Connectivity Assessment (Provinces)
description:
Imagine there are 'n' cities. Some of these cities are directly connected to each other, forming a network. Specifically, you are given an n x n adjacency matrix 'isConnected' where:
- isConnected[i][j] = 1 if city 'i' and city 'j' are directly connected.
- isConnected[i][j] = 0 otherwise.

A 'province' is defined as a group of cities that are either directly or indirectly connected through other cities in the group. No city outside the province is connected to any city within it.

Your task is to find and return the total number of distinct provinces in the network.
input_format:
The first line contains two integers n and m (where n = m for this square matrix), representing the number of cities.
The following n lines each contain n space-separated integers (0 or 1), representing the adjacency matrix 'isConnected'.
output_format: Print a single integer representing the total number of provinces.
constraints:
1 <= n <= 200
Symmetric matrix (isConnected[i][j] == isConnected[j][i])
Diagonal elements are always 1 (isConnected[i][i] == 1)
